entities.name: Estrogen contraception
observations: Combined oral contraceptive use was associated with higher total circulating 25(OH)D in several observational studies, but findings were heterogeneous across formulations and populations.
Estrogen-containing formulations may increase vitamin-D-binding protein, which can raise total 25(OH)D without increasing bioavailable 25(OH)D.

entities.name: Levonorgestrel contraception
observations: In a formulation-specific clinical study, levonorgestrel alone caused no significant change in total or bioavailable 25(OH)D.

entities.name: 25-hydroxyvitamin D
observations: Oral-contraceptive users had higher total 25(OH)D in several studies; one winter study reported 83 ± 40 versus 59 ± 22 nmol/L and a 39% adjusted difference.
Clinical formulation evidence showed smaller total 25(OH)D increases of approximately 4–7%, while bioavailable 25(OH)D could decrease.
Some studies found no significant difference or a nonsignificant decline, so the association is not universal.

entities.name: Vitamin D binding protein
observations: In users of ethinyl estradiol/levonorgestrel, vitamin-D-binding protein increased 19.1%; total 25(OH)D increased 4.4% while bioavailable 25(OH)D decreased 18.2%.

entities.name: Higher total 25(OH)D
observations: Across several human observational studies, estrogen-containing oral contraception was associated with higher total serum or plasma 25(OH)D or lower odds of hypovitaminosis D, but residual confounding and heterogeneity remain.

entities.name: Bioavailable vitamin D divergence
observations: Estrogen-containing contraception may increase total 25(OH)D through increased binding protein without increasing biologically available vitamin D; one clinical comparison found a significant decrease in bioavailable 25(OH)D with ethinyl estradiol/levonorgestrel.
